title: Esther 8
paragraphs: ¹ That same day King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther the estate of Haman, the enemy of the Jews. And Mordecai came before the king, because Esther had revealed how he was related to her. ² The king removed his signet ring — which he had reclaimed from Haman — and gave it to Mordecai. And Esther put Mordecai in charge of Haman's estate. ³ Esther again pleaded with the king, falling at his feet and weeping, begging him to stop the evil plan of Haman the Agagite and the scheme he had plotted against the Jews. ⁴ The king held out the golden scepter to Esther, and she rose and stood before him. ⁵ "If it pleases the king," she said, "and if I have found favor in his sight — if the king thinks it right and I am pleasing to him — let an order be written to revoke the letters that Haman son of Hammedatha the Agagite devised, ordering the destruction of all the Jews in every province of the king.

⁶ For how can I bear to see disaster fall on my people? How can I bear to watch the destruction of my own family?" ⁷ King Ahasuerus replied to Queen Esther and Mordecai the Jew, "I have already given Esther the estate of Haman, and he has been hanged on the gallows because he plotted against the Jews. ⁸ Now write a new decree in the king's name on behalf of the Jews as it seems best to you, and seal it with the king's signet ring — for a decree written in the king's name and sealed with his ring cannot be revoked." ⁹ The royal secretaries were summoned immediately — on the twenty-third day of the third month, the month of Sivan. They wrote out all of Mordecai's orders to the Jews, to the satraps, governors, and officials of the hundred and twenty-seven provinces stretching from India to Ethiopia, to each province in its own script and each people in their own language, and to the Jews in their own script and language. ¹⁰ He wrote in the name of King Ahasuerus, sealed the orders with the king's signet ring, and sent them by mounted couriers riding royal horses bred from the royal stud:

¹¹ The king's decree granted the Jews in every city the right to assemble and defend themselves — to destroy, kill, and annihilate any armed force of any nationality or province that might attack them or their women and children, and to plunder the property of their enemies. ¹² This was to be done in a single day throughout all the provinces of King Ahasuerus — on the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, the month of Adar. ¹³ A copy of the text of this edict was to be issued as law in every province and published to all peoples, so that the Jews would be ready to avenge themselves on their enemies on that day. ¹⁴ The couriers, riding the royal horses, rode out in haste under the king's urgent command, and the edict was also issued in Shushan the palace. ¹⁵ Mordecai left the palace wearing royal garments of blue and white, a large crown of gold, and a robe of fine linen and purple. The city of Shushan burst into joyful celebration.

¹⁶ For the Jews, it was a time of light and gladness, of joy and honor. ¹⁷ In every province and every city where the king's command and decree arrived, the Jews celebrated with joy and feasting, and declared it a holiday. And many people of other nationalities converted to Judaism, because fear of the Jews had seized them.
